posts.name: Sam Saffron
posts.cooked:
Tibo announced 28 days of shipping:

x.com

Tibo

@thsottiaux
Over the next 28 days, each day we’ll either ship one thing that is a clear improvement and relevant for most codex/work users or ship a full reset. Let the improvements begin. x.com/thsottiaux/sta…

Tibo @thsottiaux
All right, we’re locking in. Only things being worked on are simplifications, more efficiency for more usage, groundbreaking features or new models. Sometimes you have to invest ahead of the curve, but feedback is clear that you all want things to get simpler. On it.
8:33 PM - 4 Oct 2026 26K 1.5K

This post keeps track of them all!

Day Ship Announcement Details Source
1 1 Default GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol speeds increased by approximately 50%, reaching 50 rather than 30 tokens per second across subscription products and partners using Sign in With ChatGPT, with no user changes required. Details X post
2 2.1 Auto-review is free for users signed in through a ChatGPT account without consuming plan usage, uses a second agent to review potentially risky actions, and is enabled by selecting “Approve for me” in the permissions menu below the composer. Details X post
2 2.2 OpenAI simplified API rate-limit qualification from five paid usage tiers to three—Build, Launch, and Grow—and reduced the total-payment requirement for the highest tier from $1,000 to $500. Details X post
2 2.3 The Meetings plugin launched in beta for Pro and Business users in the ChatGPT macOS desktop app, taking meeting notes and saving personalized summaries and next steps in ChatGPT Space for follow-up work. Details X post
2 2.4 The Decisions API is available to all developers in public beta to choose models, tools, or actions in near real time, making decisions up to 10 times faster than GPT-6 Luna through the Responses API. Details X post
3 3 GPT-6 is in Chat, active users across Codex and ChatGPT Work reached 40 million, and a banked reset is being loaded into all paid accounts. Details X post
4 4 Instant steering lets the model react faster to adjustments for real-time course correction, and GPT-6.1 Sol ultrafast is rolling out in the API, Codex, and ChatGPT Work with near-Astra intelligence at up to 8x the speed of Sol Standard. Details X post
5 5 Composer predictions are available in beta in the Codex desktop app for Pro users, suggesting the next message based on the conversation without consuming usage. Details X post
5 5.1 Users can now create and text their dot entirely from the ChatGPT mobile app on iOS and Android. Details X post
6 6 A global reset was announced for the end of the day. — X post
7 7 The default context length for GPT-6.1 Sol in Codex and Work increased from 272k to 500k, remains configurable up to 1M, and incurs no long-context fees when usage is drawn from a subscription. — X post

posts.name: Sam Saffron
posts.cooked:
2.1 → 2.4 was deemed … not enough … by the powers that be… so we got a reset.
I think the judgement here was off codex-auto-review even just at luna 5.6 low being 100% free, is both wide open for abuse and significant cause it makes approve for me a super easy decision to make.

Decisions API to me is a bit anticlimactic cause there is a glut of these around, many of which are much faster (including open source models). I am sure it will get there after a few iterations.

posts.name: Mb
posts.cooked:
Just when I finally had some time to test Astra 6.0, things are already moving on. Everything is evolving so quickly these days—I’m struggling to keep up! But I guess that is good sign.

“… either ship one thing that is a clear improvement and relevant for most codex/work users or ship a full reset.” — I agree ^00

“We have made Auto-review free for all users signed in through a ChatGPT account. You can enable it in settings > permissions > auto-review. Auto-review improves upon the default sandbox setting that requires you to approve everything, which is prone to decision fatigue unless you spend a lot of time configuring specific rules.” – Isn’t it … settings > code review > automatic review ?

“Never worry about remembering what you were saying with that colleague. Just talk your heart out and build up the context to load up into codex to get it all done.” – I was actually using GPT Audio for this before, but good feature to add.

posts.name: Sam Saffron
posts.cooked:
sam.saffron:

Instant steering

I was curious about this one:

github.com/openai/codex

Enable instant interrupts by default (#51812)

main ← copyberry/codex-internal-to-codex-oss/a8cab2d6c445bfdbd10b0b2abcf7893d32ee8595
opened 07:42PM - 07 Oct 26 UTC
copyberry[bot]
+33 -5

Enable instant interrupts by default ## What changed Enable `instant_interrupt…` by default so new user input can preempt responses and yield foreground code-mode observations. Keep the feature marked as under development and update feature-policy tests to allow this exception. Explicitly disable instant interrupts in core, TUI, and Python SDK tests that depend on responses completing before steering or processing subsequent input.

Old behavior

Mid turn messages went into pending_input, added to next sampling step.

New behavior:

When an interruption comes in a new undocumented:

{"type": "response.interrupt", "response_id": "...", "mode": "discard_partial_items"}

Is sent. Additionally, code mode has a clean way of yielding in long code mode blocks per: Enable code mode interruption by default by copyberry[bot] · Pull Request #51835 · openai/codex · GitHub

This is a nice feature, waiting on steering can be annoying, that said… there is a big piece of nuance here.

Got to use x-openai-internal-codex-responses-lite: true for this to work.

Now… the price you pay for this at least from source in codex.

Codex ties the fate of this feature with disabling of parallel tool calls.

For most harnesses this would be a disaster, but codex is moving more and more work into codemode so parallel tool calls are not needed as much.

Curious to see how this plays out, for image gen this is very nice, for other cases … it is a tricky compromise.

From API probing:

image1048×1347 131 KB

Parallel tool calls MUST be disabled and responses lite enabled for discard_partial_items to work.

posts.name: Codex-Reset.com
posts.cooked:
Wow, that’s wild. AI is insanely efficient these days—but is this really what we want?

Anyway, what I most want to know is: when’s the new model dropping?
Really useful roundup! I’m looking forward to seeing what gets announced over the next few days.

posts.name: Sam Saffron
posts.cooked:
sam.saffron:

The default context length for GPT-6.1 Sol in Codex and Work increased from 272k to 500k, remains configurable up to 1M, and incurs no long-context fees when usage is drawn from a subscription.

To me this is an anti-feature. Your quota will run out faster and we all know that you will not get as good needle in the haystack on 500k vs 272k.

Compaction at 272k to me feels fine from everyday use. I know I can set to whatever I want, but the gift of running out of limits faster for a few less compactions seems like an anti gift to me.
